name: Squid Fry (Calamari)
instructions: 1. Clean the squid thoroughly, remove the ink sac and membranes, then cut into uniform rings.
2. Marinate the rings with turmeric, chili powder, pepper, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt for 30 minutes.
3. Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
4. Add the fennel seeds and curry leaves, letting them splutter to release their aroma.
5. Add the marinated squid rings and sliced onions to the pan.
6. Sauté on high heat for 3-5 minutes, ensuring the squid cooks quickly to remain tender; do not overcook as it becomes rubbery.
7. Serve hot as a snack or side dish with steamed rice.
description: Squid Fry is a staple in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, reflecting the region's abundant access to fresh seafood. It is heavily influenced by South Indian and Bengali culinary traditions, characterized by the use of coconut oil and aromatic spices that highlight the natural sweetness of the fresh catch.
